content.title: Levi's Denim, Campaigns Drive Higher Sales
content.description: Despite Levi Strauss & Co.'s updated earnings guidance falling short of investor expectations, namely earnings growth failing to match the pace of sale expansion, CFO Harmit Singh believes that, overall, the company is strong, defined by "accelerated growth, expanding margins, and higher return on invested capital." He joined Carol Massar and Bailey Lipschultz on 'Bloomberg Businessweek Daily' to discuss denim sales and the impacts of tariffs.

content.title: Stocks Priced Near Perfection as Analyst Profit Sentiment Wanes
content.summary: A Citigroup Inc. index tracking US earnings revisions — the number of analysts upgrading versus downgrading estimates — has turned flat for the first time since August.  At the same time, the S&P 500 is trading at 22 times forward earnings, above the average over the past decade of nearly 19 times.  The third-quarter season will pick up steam from Tuesday with reports from banks including JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Citigroup.

content.title: Levi’s (LEVI) Profit Margin More Than Triples, Reinforcing Bullish Earnings Narratives
content.summary: Levi Strauss (LEVI) posted a powerful year, with net profit jumping 226.1% from last year and achieving a net profit margin of 7.9%, up significantly from 2.7%. The pace of projected earnings growth, at 10.55% per year, lags the broader US market but still signals a steady expansion outlook for both revenue and profits.
